title: The split from tinytown left broken reads: tools/lessons-check exits 1, cli/tests/tiny.rs reds 7 of 9 (two surrounding-project paths, five on .DS_Store the pack check refuses), docs describe a Makefile and budget that did not come over, tinytown roster names in fixtures
description:
## Why

The move from tinytown (2026-09-22, commit 44c3736) left pieces of the tree still reading paths and infrastructure that stayed in tinytown. Found during the post-split bead sweep (2026-09-23). Closed on this bead's behalf: fleet-40zjb, fleet-j8v9u and fleet-wrmw0 (the old boundary scan). Their close reasons point here for what is left.

## What is broken (measured 2026-09-23)

1. tools/lessons-check exits 1: "no tracked file under fleet/brain/lessons — nothing to check". It hard-codes fleet/brain/lessons (lines 2, 221, 223; the documents are now at brain/lessons/) and reads seats/README.md for roster needles, which is tinytown-only. The migration had already removed its tree-wide boundary scan (FOREIGN_TOKEN, SELF_ALLOWED).
2. cargo nextest run -p fleet-cli --test tiny: 7 of 9 fail.
   - no_file_in_the_pack_carries_an_item_id_from_the_surrounding_project: foreign_token() (cli/tests/tiny.rs:84) reads <parent of repo>/fleet/tools/lessons-check for FOREIGN_TOKEN, which no longer exists anywhere.
   - no_file_in_the_pack_names_a_seat_of_the_surrounding_project: roster_needles() (tiny.rs:152) reads <parent of repo>/seats/README.md.
   - The other five fail on untracked macOS .DS_Store files under packs/ (packs/.DS_Store, packs/tiny/.DS_Store, packs/tiny/skills/.DS_Store, packs/ts/.DS_Store). pack_files() (tiny.rs:44) reads every file as UTF-8, and the pack check itself refuses "unknown top-level name `.DS_Store`" and "`skills/.DS_Store` holds no SKILL.md". THE SECOND HALF IS A PRODUCT BUG, NOT A TEST BUG: fleet's pack validation will refuse any pack a macOS Finder has opened. It may deserve its own bead.
3. The docs describe infrastructure that did not come over. README.md "Working here" lists make fleet-fmt/check/test/ring and a budget in "the surrounding project's own policy file". The header comments of .config/nextest.toml name "the Makefile's wrapper", a budget in fleet.toml and fleet/tools/suite-profile. Whether a runner and budget come back is fleet-6ravv's open question; until then the docs should describe what exists.
4. Tinytown roster names remain as fixture strings: "Rook" and "Wren" in about 17 files (controller/src/sessions.rs, cli/tests/drive_effects.rs, controller/tests/observe.rs, …) and "architect-1" at core/tests/dispatch.rs:28. They are harmless as fixtures but name another project's seats. Scrub them before the repo is public (Alberto's D5: a cleanup pass after the migration).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 tools/lessons-check runs green against brain/lessons/, with the tinytown-only roster source removed or replaced by a local list.
- AC2 cargo nextest run -p fleet-cli --test tiny is 9/9 green on a macOS box that has .DS_Store files under packs/. The two surrounding-project arms are either deleted (the boundary they guarded is gone) or re-pointed at something that exists in this repo.
- AC3 fleet's pack check ignores OS litter (.DS_Store at least) or refuses it deliberately with a named reason. State which, and add an arm.
- AC4 README.md and the .config/nextest.toml header describe only what exists in this repo.
- AC5 git grep -n -E 'Rook|Wren|architect-[0-9]' outside .beads/ reads 0, or each survivor is justified in the landing.

title: fleet seat nudge addresses a named seat by its directory while the live session answers to its chosen name, and writes outcome sent on a failed send — chosen_name on the six [seats.*] tables, and the outcome read from the turn's output
description:
## Why

Measured 2026-09-22T16:25Z and 16:27Z during the switch sitting's pre-flight (tinytown-tnkuq.23, runbook step 09): `fleet seat nudge builder-1 --text …` wrote session.nudged with outcome "sent" twice, and Rook received nothing. The print-mode turn's own log at ~/.fleet/nudges/builder-1-1790094337204.log reads: "Send failed. No agent named `builder-1` is reachable. Available sessions: crane, kestrel, jay, wren, daw, rook." Two defects, one cause each.

1. THE NUDGE ADDRESSES A NAME NOBODY ANSWERS TO. fleet/cli/src/item.rs:1221 sets the display name to row.chosen_name or else row.name, and fleet/controller/src/effect.rs:105 does the same for the controller's own nudge. tinytown's fleet.toml carries no chosen_name key on any [seats.*] table (grep, 0 hits) and ~/.fleet/config.json's eight rows carry none, so every nudge to a named seat addresses the seat directory ("builder-1") while the live session registered itself under its chosen name ("rook") at wake. Transient seats are unaffected because their chosen name is their directory, which is why the 2026-09-14 nudge to transient-4 delivered.

2. THE VERB WRITES "sent" ON A FAILED SEND. fleet/controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs:505 reads the print-mode turn's exit status, and the turn exits 0 after reporting the send failed, so RingOutcome::Delivered and session.nudged outcome "sent" are written over a message nobody received. A dispatch cannot witness its own success (brain/builder-manual.md rule); the witness is the log's own "Send failed" line or the send return the turn was told to report.

## What lands

- The six named seats' [seats.*] tables in fleet.toml gain chosen_name = "Wren" | "Crane" | "Rook" | "Daw" | "Jay" | "Kestrel", matching seats/README.md's roster (rows 27 to 32); fleet start re-renders them into config.json through render_seats (fleet/controller/src/lifecycle.rs:428, which updates rows on every start, unlike write_seat_list which writes only the first).
- The nudge's outcome reads the turn's OUTPUT for the send's own result: a log carrying "Send failed" is RingOutcome::Failed with that line as the cause, whatever the exit status, and session.nudged records outcome "failed: …". Its red proof: a stub agent whose print-mode turn prints "Send failed" and exits 0 must produce a failed outcome.
- The policy checker (fleet.toml's readers, tools/fleet-policy or the drift suite) reds a managed named seat whose table carries no chosen_name, so the gap cannot re-open when a seat is added.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 fleet seat nudge builder-1 --text "ping" delivers: the nudge log carries the send return and no "Send failed", and Rook's session shows the message.
- AC2 The stub arm: exit 0 with "Send failed" in the output reads outcome "failed" on the stream; the mutant that reads exit status alone reds it.
- AC3 fleet start over a config.json whose rows lack chosen_name prints "N row(s) rendered — 0 added, 6 updated" and the rows carry the names.
- Gate: touched suites green; reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

## Sequencing

Before the switch sitting's S3: the handoff nudges of step 09 depend on it. One bead wide.
notes:
Moved from the tinytown board on 2026-09-22, where it was tinytown-fmver; that bead is closed there with a pointer here. Edges to beads that stayed on the tinytown board, not carried across: discovered-from tinytown-tnkuq.23.
POST-SPLIT CORRECTION (2026-09-23 sweep, checked against HEAD 44c3736). Scope update. Defect 2 is still live: controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs:505-506 maps any exit 0 to Ok, cli/src/item.rs:1231 makes that RingOutcome::Delivered, and cli/src/nudge.rs:76 writes 'sent'; nothing reads 'Send failed'. Keep AC2 as the core of this bead. Defect 1's code side is unchanged (cli/src/item.rs:1221 and controller/src/effect.rs:105 fall back to row.name), but the six chosen_name keys are tinytown instance data (its fleet.toml and ~/.fleet/config.json), and tools/fleet-policy did not come over: drop that edit and AC1 from this repo's scope. In-repo replacement: warn in lifecycle render_seats, or in a policy.rs read, when a managed named seat has no chosen_name. New finding: the cli passes chosen_name un-lowercased (item.rs:1221) while the controller lowercases it (effect.rs:106-109). The 'before S3' sequencing is stale.

title: a gh rerun is a fourth production surface the pack does not carry: the reference refuses every rerun and fleet allows one, measured at tinytown-tnkuq.76
description:
## Why

Measured on tinytown-tnkuq.76 by driving both guards with the same payload
table, 23 rows: every row agrees except one.

  gh run rerun 12345  ->  fleet allowed, reference REFUSED

.claude/hooks/prod-write-guard.py's gh_finding refuses EVERY rerun, and says
why in its own docstring: resolving a run id to its workflow and its ref needs
a network call, so the guard cannot tell a rerun of a backend/release run from
any other, and it refuses the class rather than let the one through. A rerun of
a backend/release run re-deploys all four backend services to prd; of a
web/release run, the web app.

tinytown-tnkuq.76 carried the three surfaces its spec named — prod_make_goals,
prod_dagger_functions, prod_workflow_refs — and a rerun is a FOURTH, which that
bead's 'What lands' does not name. It was left unbuilt deliberately rather than
invented: unlike the other three there is no list to read, so refusing a rerun
is a policy decision about a whole verb rather than a target match, and that is
the architect's to make rather than a builder's.

## What is unanswered

At the switch (tinytown-tnkuq.23) the hook leaves with .claude/hooks, and this
surface goes unguarded. Three shapes were put beside each other and none is
taken here:

1. A fourth check that refuses every `gh run rerun` whenever prod_workflow_refs
   is non-empty — the reference's own shape, carried. Over-refuses a rerun of a
   non-production run, which the escape covers.
2. A declared list of rerun-guarded repositories or workflows, matching the
   other three keys' shape. Reads a run id this class cannot resolve, so it
   would refuse on the repository rather than on the run.
3. Leave it out and state the residual on the class, as the class already
   states the reader's own residuals.

## Acceptance Criteria

• AC1 the shape is ruled by an architect and the ruling written on this bead
  before any code lands.
• AC2 whichever shape is taken, the agreement table of tinytown-tnkuq.76 item 4
  is re-run and the rerun row agrees, or the row is stated as an accepted
  residual on fleet/core/src/guard/production_write.rs's header with the
  reference's own line cited.

covers: none
notes:
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-22T04:26:14Z read from date -u, the DECISION LOG for tinytown-hdedm pasted in architect-2's session, mechanism: gh-rerun-refused-whole, verbatim): "D3: A" — option A as put on the flight report: a fourth check that refuses every gh run rerun whenever prod_workflow_refs is non-empty, the reference hook's own shape carried, with the escape covering a rerun of a non-production run. This bead's AC1 is met by this line: the shape is ruled and written before any code lands. What follows is a build — the fourth check in fleet/core/src/guard/production_write.rs under the workflow-ref list, one arm with its control and its escape, and AC2's agreement table re-run so the rerun row agrees — which is a spec pass away from the pool; the kind:decide label comes off when that spec is written, because the work is no longer the decision.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-22, in chat in architect-1's session through AskUserQuestion at 2026-09-22T15:18:06Z, mechanism: gh-rerun-lands-after-the-switch, verbatim): "After, as a residual (Recommended)"
What follows: the switch sitting (tinytown-tnkuq.23) does not wait on this bead. Its S6 step, which deletes .claude/hooks and with it the reference's rerun refusal, carries the residual in the record: reruns of a backend/release or web/release run are unguarded from S6 until this bead lands, and that window is stated on fleet/core/src/guard/production_write.rs's header at S6 with the reference's own line cited, as AC2's residual form already allows. This bead lands on the first flight after the switch; it still owes its spec pass (the fourth check under the workflow-ref list, one arm with its control and its escape, AC2's table re-run), and kind:decide comes off then. Option put beside it and not taken: before the switch, one spec pass and one landing under a small direct flight with the switch waiting on it.
Moved from the tinytown board on 2026-09-22, where it was tinytown-xxyn6; that bead is closed there with a pointer here. Edges to beads that stayed on the tinytown board, not carried across: discovered-from tinytown-tnkuq.76; relates-to tinytown-tnkuq.23.
POST-SPLIT CORRECTION (2026-09-23 sweep, checked against HEAD 44c3736). Still true: grep -i rerun core/src/guard reads 0 and CHECKS has six entries. The residual line the 2026-09-22 ruling promised for the production_write header was never written, so state it now. The reference hook .claude/hooks/prod-write-guard.py is deleted everywhere; for AC2's agreement table read it from tinytown history at fb4537d18~1:.claude/hooks/prod-write-guard.py. Paths drop fleet/. Gate commands: there is no Makefile here (see fleet-6ravv), so make fleet-fmt/check/test mean cargo fmt --all --check / cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets / cargo nextest run --workspace from the repo root; make lessons-check is broken until fleet-mdw lands.

title: The ratchet's step back: bring make fleet-test under 350 s again (fleet-cli::plan at 150 arm-seconds over five arms first, then seat and deliver) and return suites.fleet_test_budget_seconds from 370 to 350 in the same landing — the second trim Alberto's raise-once ruling on tinytown-88kg5 orders
description:
## Why

Alberto's ruling on tinytown-88kg5 (2026-09-18, fleet-test-budget-raised-once-to-370) raised suites.fleet_test_budget_seconds from 350 to 370 once, on the condition that the ratchet's step back is filed in the same act. This is that step: the key's contract (tinytown-6ravv.6) is that it only goes down, and this bead is what brings it back.

## What was measured

After tinytown-88kg5's trim, make fleet-test on a quiet box reads 364.4 and 365.4 s (989 arms, four threads). The junit of that run ranks the binaries by arm-seconds: fleet-cli::seat 185.0 over 24 arms, fleet-cli::plan 149.6 over five arms (about 30 s each, on a solo board), fleet-cli::deliver 131.1 over ten, fleet-cli::run 125.7 over eleven. The remaining cost in the run suite is bd process startups inside the verbs (about 1.5 s each against the run's dolt server), which no rig trim reaches; the same is likely true of plan and deliver, whose arms drive the shipped binary through real boards.

## What this bead asks

Bring make fleet-test back under 350 s on a quiet box and set the key back to 350 in the same landing. Start with fleet-cli::plan (the densest: five arms, 30 s each, a solo board — measure whether the board or the verbs' bd round trips carry it), then seat and deliver, with the junit before and after quoted per binary. Where the cost is the verb's own bd calls, say so with the count and stop: that becomes a finding on the verb, not a rig edit. Rig-only changes; no assertion dropped without a D line saying which and why.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 make fleet-test reads within 350 s on two consecutive quiet runs (load-before under 5.0), every arm green, with the test-phase lines quoted.
- AC2 suites.fleet_test_budget_seconds reads 350 in the landing, and the key's comment names this bead as the step back.
- AC3 the junit before and after, per binary touched, quoted on the bead; every mutant the trimmed binaries' beads named still kills what it killed.

covers: none — a test-rig trim builds no requirement
notes:
On flight tinytown-6bphr — filed by the operator (architect-1) at 2026-09-18T14:38:39Z as the ratchet step Alberto's ruling on tinytown-88kg5 orders. STOWED, UNFED: rides to the desk on the flight report as the next flight's first row candidate. Not ordered: no orders key, no feed marker.

LEVER ADDED (2026-09-18T18:44:30Z, from tinytown-z4pdc's delivery on flight tinytown-6bphr): fleet-cli::item_json joins the table — 8 arms at 121.6 to 128.2 arm-seconds in the full suite before the trim, 5 arms at about 94 (binary alone, served) after; the builder's measurement says the remaining cost is arms-in-flight x bd calls x per-call latency (0.3 to 0.4 s alone, 1.2 to 2 s with four arms queued on the one engine), so the two levers left are a serial test-group for binary(item_json) in fleet/.config/nextest.toml (arms in flight to one; predicted 25 to 30 arm-seconds; it changes how the suite schedules and is the operator's call, not a builder's) and the in-process seam (fleet-zs4y1). The same shape holds for seat, plan, deliver, run, autopilot and dispatch: each verb's own bd calls, not the board init. Prior readings on this bead stand.
Moved from the tinytown board on 2026-09-22, where it was tinytown-e6t4e; that bead is closed there with a pointer here. Edges to beads that stayed on the tinytown board, not carried across: discovered-from tinytown-88kg5.

description:
tinytown-6ravv.14 landed its MECHANISM and one arm, then closed. The conversion
work its spec names is not done and, at filing time, stood in no open bead —
which is why this exists. Filed by the seat that reviewed and landed .14.

  engine's last seven hard-wired pieces (fly git, land git, spawner, ring,
  seats, lane, load) behind a seam, RealRigging shipped, the shipped path's
  construction order and its `?` positions verified unchanged by the reviewer.
  Four cfg(test) arms proving the seam, plus ONE converted arm:
  autopilot_opens_the_oldest_plan_and_the_next_only_after_the_first_closes_in_process,
  178.5 s -> 0.072 s, with its out-of-process original deleted.

THE NUMBERS, with the tree each was taken on, because two pairs are in
circulation and they are NOT interchangeable:

This one converts the arms that are NOT ring. They are separable and the lane

title: fleet's flight suite hangs in a_loop_killed_between_a_dispatch_and_its_event on a fleet fly fixture that never returns, unbounded by nextest or test-tools — twice on this box in one day, once holding the lane's rerun for two hours
description:
## Why, re-measured on origin/main 10d77b2d2

Two beads described one fixture: this one (filed 2026-09-14 off the rehearsal, no SHA pinned, the child at 0% CPU) and tinytown-b456a (filed 2026-09-15 by builder-2 at 93bccaa85 on an idle box, the child ticking bd once a second, 7.86 s of CPU over 1h43m). They are folded here; b456a's measurement is transcribed in its close and its record stays readable. This bead's earlier crate attribution was wrong: the arm lives only in fleet/cli/tests/flight.rs, at 1883 (a_loop_killed_between_a_dispatch_and_its_event_restarts_without_dispatching_twice); fleet/core/tests/flight.rs holds no such arm.

What the arm does: Rig::run (flight.rs:773) spawns the shipped binary with Command::output(), blocking, no Child, no deadline; the first fly is killed by a file seam (kill_the_loop_when_the_item_is_assigned, :735), and the resumed fly at :1921 is the unbounded call. The resumed fly is item.rs:332-342: is_open and no running controller, so fly_in_the_foreground (fleet/cli/src/flights.rs:341) — a loop that reads the record, returns when its status is not open, otherwise calls advance_one and sleeps poll_seconds (1 s in the rig's fleet.toml, flight.rs:165), and whose only exit is the record closing (flights.rs:361-364); a refusal from advance_one is written to stderr and the loop asks again (366-370). So the two signatures on the record are two different faults: a child at 0% CPU is a wedge inside one advance (a child of the advance never returning); a child ticking once a second is an advance that refuses every pass, and the reason is on the fixture's captured stderr line by line.

The profile half this bead once asked for is landed: fleet/.config/nextest.toml carries slow-timeout period 330s, terminate-after 2, grace-period 5s (tinytown-6ravv.5 and .6; a 30 s period killed 141 arms and was withdrawn), so the arm now reads TIMEOUT by name at 660 s instead of hanging a lane. This bead's earlier Implementation part (1) claimed fleet fly already accepts a deadline; it does not — fly_in_the_foreground takes out, err, here and flight and nothing else, and FlyArgs carries no timeout.

## What

1. The fixture half: Rig gains a bounded fly — the resumed fleet fly spawned as a Child owned by a guard whose Drop kills its process group, waited on with a deadline the arm names (120 s), and on the deadline the arm fails printing the fixture's event stream, the builder log and the child's captured stderr, never hangs. Rig::run's other uses stay as they are.
2. The diagnosis, delivered whichever way it comes out: the arm run at tip ten times through fleet/tools/soak at load under 5; on a deadline hit, the captured stderr says which of the two signatures it is and why (a refusal line per second names the advance's stop; silence names the wedge), and the cause is fixed in the same delivery if it is in the flight path (fleet/cli/src/flights.rs, fleet/core/src/item/advance.rs) or filed with the stderr quoted if it is elsewhere.
3. No change to fleet/.config/nextest.toml; the profile half is landed and its period is measured, not this bead's to move.

## Acceptance Criteria

AC1 The arm green ten of ten through soak at load under 5 on the delivered tree, wall under 60 s each, table quoted.
AC2 Red proof of the bound: with the fix of item 2 reverted (or the kill seam left armed), the arm fails at its own deadline within 130 s, printing the event stream and the last stderr lines; it never reaches nextest's 660 s TIMEOUT. Quoted.
AC3 No fleet fly process outlives the suite: the process table read before and after a full run of fleet-cli::flight, quoted, the guard's Drop having killed the group on the failing arm of AC2.
AC4 The cause of the ticking signature, named from the captured stderr, with the fix and its own red proof; or, if the ten runs at tip never reproduce it, the ten stderr captures kept and the signature filed as not reproduced at tip with the base SHAs it was seen at.
AC5 cargo nextest list: fleet-cli::flight 8 arms both sides; make fleet-check exits 0.

Gate line: touched suites green; reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.
covers: none — tooling under the fleet-tests epic, no PRD requirement; the delivery note carries the same line.

## Sequencing

Blocked by tinytown-a221k (the repeat-runner AC1 and AC4 count with); the edge is on the record. On flight 14's board; tinytown-b456a's flight 13 row comes off the board with its close.

---

## As filed, before the spec pass (verbatim)

## Why

Found at the rehearsal's step 19 (tinytown-tnkuq.20, 2026-09-14): the lane's rerun of `make test-tools` for tinytown-f79ck ran serially (width 1) and hung for over two hours inside the fleet workspace's test `a_loop_killed_between_a_dispatch_and_its_event_restarts_with…` (fleet/core, the flight suite, binary flight-3ad377a842b237c5): the test process sat at 0% CPU with a child `fleet fly fx-9aa --by architect-1` from the lane's own debug build, also at 0% CPU, for 2h19m. The controller was blocked in the landing step the whole time and the projection went stale. The same fixture shape was found at step 06 before the sitting: a `fleet fly fx-13o --by architect-1` from builder-2's worktree, twenty hours old, in a fleet-cli-flight-shape-fly temp project — ended by Alberto's ruling. The operator ended the lane's one to let the rerun finish.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `make fleet-test` (or the lane's `make test-tools`) on this box and watch `pgrep -fl 'fleet fly'` during the flight suite.
2. Observe the arm `a_loop_killed_between_a_dispatch_and_its_event_restarts_with…` holding with a child `fleet fly fx-<id> --by architect-1` at 0% CPU (2h19m on 2026-09-14 in the lane; 20h on builder-2's worktree the day before).
3. Kill the fixture: the arm ends and the suite finishes.
4. Expected: the arm passes or fails within a bound, and no `fleet fly` outlives the suite.

## What was measured

`fleet fly` "decides whether to run the advance in the foreground" off the projection (fleet/controller/src/seat.rs, the collector check), and the test drives it under a scratch machine directory; whatever it waited on never came, and nothing bounded it: nextest ran with no slow-timeout terminate for this workspace, and tools/test-tools bounds a row by nothing either. Two occurrences on this box in one day, both `--by architect-1` — the test reads the ambient actor — and both surviving their suite.

## What

The test's fly is run with a bound (the flight PRD's foreground advance takes a timeout; the test passes one), and the workspace's nextest config carries a slow-timeout with terminate-after so a hung arm reads as a failure with the test's name instead of a suite that never ends. A fixture that spawns `fleet fly` cleans it up on drop.

## Implementation

Where: the fleet flight suite's arm `a_loop_killed_between_a_dispatch_and_its_event_restarts_with…` (fleet/core, the flight tests binary) runs `fleet fly` in a rig; `fleet fly` decides whether to run the advance in the foreground off the projection (fleet/controller/src/seat.rs, the collector check) and, in the rig's shape, waited forever. Nothing bounded it: fleet/.config/nextest.toml carries no slow-timeout with terminate-after, and tools/test-tools bounds a row by nothing.

Change, three parts. (1) The rig's fly takes the deadline `fleet fly` already accepts for its foreground advance (or the test passes one) so the fixture returns within seconds when the collector is absent. (2) The rig's spawned `fleet fly` child is owned by a guard whose `Drop` kills it, so a failing arm leaks nothing. (3) fleet/.config/nextest.toml gains `slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 3 }` for the workspace, so a hung arm reads FAILED with its name inside three minutes. The read-only census before and after the suite (`pgrep -fl 'fleet fly'`) is the acceptance's instrument.

Test: the arm itself passes within the bound; a deliberate arm whose fly waits on a collector that never comes reads FAILED by the timeout, not hung. Red proof: the Drop guard removed, the process table after the suite holds a `fleet fly`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The fleet workspace suite finishes on this box with no `fleet fly` process outliving it, proved by a process-table read before and after; a hung arm reads FAILED with its name within the configured bound.
- A red proof: the bound removed, a fly made to wait forever holds the suite past the bound.
- Gate: touched suites green; reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

title: a resumed item orders the retire of the seat that parked it, which the park already retired, and the refusal on the missing row stops the whole flight pass every tick
description:
## Re-measured 2026-09-16 (author, tree b2db5ee27) — read first; it corrects the call site and the test's mechanic

fleet/core/src/item/advance.rs is byte-identical to the spec's base, and the diagnosis stands: fn retire at :2741 carries a seam refusal as could-not-tell (:2748), and the act at :353-354 aborts the flight's whole pass on it; the string is made at fleet/controller/src/transient.rs:253 (moved from :248 by tinytown-m7u8t). Two corrections. (1) THE CALL SITE: the resume path in dispatch_act orders no retire — it withdraws the stale order (:518, withdraw, tinytown-tnkuq.50) — so the retire a resumed item can order comes from resumed() in flight.rs:245 taking the item to Accepted and accepted_act (:1643) calling retire_the_reviewer (:1870, the retire at :1881), or from parked_act (:444-447); retire has eight call sites (:447, :775, :997, :1183, :1210, :1333, :1623, :1881). (2) THE TEST'S MECHANIC: "when the fold shows a session.retired after the seat's last session.spawned" cannot work, because state_of slices the stream at this flight's opened seq (fleet/core/src/item/flight.rs:302, records with seq greater than opened), so the previous flight's retire is outside the fold's window. The check reads the WHOLE stream, call.records (advance.rs:234-238 carries it; the cli reads it from seq 0 at fleet/cli/src/flights.rs:617): a retire whose seat's last session.spawned is followed by a session.retired anywhere in the stream is Retired::default(), which means fn retire takes the records, threaded through its eight call sites, or the check is made once in the act that orders it. The AC's observable follows the call site: on the Accepted path the arm reads a landing, not item.dispatched; the builder names which path the arm drives and reads that path's event. Everything else stands.

---

## Why

Found at the rehearsal's step 19 (tinytown-tnkuq.20, 2026-09-14): the four items parked on flight tinytown-41z31 were answered and planned again as tinytown-0cco6, and its first pass refused every tick from 10:33Z: "the flight pass refused: tinytown-0cco6: `transient-1` could not be retired: `transient-1` is not a row of this machine's seat list". Nothing on the flight moved.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fly an item whose builder asks a question (`fleet ask`); the item parks and the seat is retired (`session.retired` on the stream, its row dropped).
2. `fleet answer` the gate, plan the item again, `fleet fly`.
3. Read service.err.log: "the flight pass refused: <flight>: `<seat>` could not be retired: `<seat>` is not a row of this machine's seat list" on every tick; nothing on the flight moves.
4. Expected: the resumed item dispatches on the first pass with no retire refusal.

## What was measured

fleet/core/src/item/advance.rs `retire`: a seat that will not retire stops the act rather than being skipped (R12's obligation — a landing over an unreclaimed seat would hold memory for the flight's life). The resumed item's record names the seat that parked it (transient-1 asked the question on tinytown-veapf at 2175909c6972), and that seat was ALREADY retired at the park — session.retired transient-1 at 08:55:03Z, its row dropped from config.json, its worktree removed. On resume the advance orders the retire again, the controller's seat seam answers "not a row", and the could-not-tell refuses the whole pass, so a flight of four ready items is held by a seat that no longer exists. The retire at the park and the retire at the resume are two orders for one reclaim.

## What

A retire ordered on resume reads the record first: a seat whose retire already landed (session.retired on the stream, or no row and no worktree) is Retired::default() and not a refusal; only a seat that is still held and will not release stops the act. R12 is met once per seat, not once per order.

## Implementation

Where: fleet/core/src/item/advance.rs, `retire` (the seam call whose refusal is carried as could-not-tell, line 2748) — ordered when a parked-then-answered item resumes, naming the seat that parked it; that seat was already retired at the park (`session.retired` on the stream, no row, no worktree).

Change: the `Seats` seam's retire answers a distinct kind for "not a row" (fleet/controller/src/transient.rs line 248 is where the string is made); in `retire`, that kind is `Ok(Retired::default())` when the fold shows a `session.retired` for the seat after its last `session.spawned` — the reclaim already happened — and stays a `Stop` otherwise (a seat that is held and will not release is still R12's obligation). The resume path then proceeds to its dispatch in the same pass.

Test, in advance's tests: park an item on a question through the rig, retire its seat as the park does, answer, plan again, and read `item.dispatched` on the first pass of the new flight with no could-not-tell in the log; a second arm where the seat is NOT on the stream as retired keeps the refusal. Red proof: the record check removed, the first arm reads the refusal every pass, as flight tinytown-0cco6 did.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A parked-then-answered item whose parking seat was retired at the park resumes on the next plan without a retire refusal, proved by an arm that parks, retires, answers, plans and reads item.dispatched.
- A red proof: the record check removed, the arm reads the could-not-tell.
- Gate: touched suites green; reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

title: a reviewer spawn the machine belt refuses for load parks the item behind a human gate instead of holding until the load falls — two of four rehearsal items parked on a condition that cleared in minutes
description:
## Re-measured 2026-09-16 (author, tree b2db5ee27) — four corrections

(1) The belt's reason string changed under this spec: fleet/controller/src/transient.rs:456 now prints "load average (5m)" and :308 reads platform::load_average_5m (tinytown-6ravv.3, a7f9631f9); the Why and Steps sections below quote the one-minute string the tree no longer prints — the mechanism is unchanged, the words are. (2) The seam is Spawner, not Seats: fleet/core/src/item/mod.rs:341-344 SpawnOutcome::Refused(String) carries no kind, which is still the gap this spec closes; Seats (advance.rs:178-190) carries worktree, feed and retire only. (3) There are THREE park sites, not two: the reviewer spawn (:1546-1560), the return's builder spawn (:1778-1799) and the crash re-dispatch (:872). (4) The doctrine citation was wrong: brain/builder-manual.md carries no belt rule, and brain/architect-role.md states the belt as a refusal; the real precedent for "a belt refusal is a hold" is IN THE CODE — advance.rs:584-590, the dispatch path, which already holds and retries a belt-refused spawn in list order (R9), with its arm at fleet/core/tests/advance.rs:1097. So the change is: make the three sites behave as the dispatch site does, with the kind carried on SpawnOutcome so a belt refusal is told from every other. Two things the spec did not budget: hold_passes exists nowhere (fleet, fleet.toml: zero hits; adding it means the census at fleet/core/src/policy.rs:39-58 and its arm at fleet/core/tests/policy.rs:46-60), and the two-pass belt arm (refused on the first pass, admitted on the second) needs StubSpawner to queue a sequence of answers — it answers once today (tests/advance.rs:166, :207). The existing arm a_reviewer_the_belt_refused_parks_with_the_refusal_as_the_question (tests/advance.rs:3201) argues the opposite of this spec and is AMENDED by it, not merely joined.

---

## Why

Found at the rehearsal's step 18 (tinytown-tnkuq.20, 2026-09-14): tinytown-x7x9q delivered at 08:33:09Z and tinytown-z89ga at 08:36:11Z, each build step passed, each builder retired clean — and each item was PARKED two seconds later (item.parked at seq 61 and 70, gates tinytown-9047i and tinytown-h105j, type human) with the reason "no reviewer could be spawned at <commit> — the machine cannot take another transient seat: load average over its ceiling. load average (1m): 23.84 (ceiling 10.00 = 10 cpu x 1.00); transient seats mid-turn: 3 (cap 3)". The load was the other builders' own suites (tinytown-tnkuq.86) and fell under the ceiling within minutes of their deliveries.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fly two or more items while the box's one-minute load is over the ceiling (ten times the cpu count divided by ten; here 10.00) — four builders running full suites suffices.
2. When an item is delivered, read the stream: `item.parked` two seconds after `item.delivered` with the reason "no reviewer could be spawned at <commit> — the machine cannot take another transient seat: load average over its ceiling" and a human gate on the item.
3. Wait for the load to fall under the ceiling: nothing resumes; `fleet answer` and a new plan are needed.
4. Expected: the item stays delivered and the reviewer spawns on the first pass under the ceiling.

## What was measured

The machine belt (fleet/controller/src/transient.rs, the refusal built from the load ceiling and the transient cap) is a reading about THIS MINUTE — load, seats mid-turn — and the advance treats its refusal at the reviewer's spawn as a park: a human gate on the item, the flight's record moved to parked, the item resumed only by an answer and a later plan. The belt in this project's doctrine is a WAIT (brain/builder-manual.md; the load-belt rule on brain/architect-role.md): a spawn refused for load is retried when the load falls, and nobody is asked anything. Two of four items now need the morning ritual and a second takeoff to be reviewed, for a condition that cleared itself.

## What

A belt refusal at a spawn is a HOLD, not a park: the advance leaves the item at delivered, notes the refusal with its two readings, and retries the spawn on a later pass; the park is reserved for a refusal that a later pass cannot clear (the cap on returns or crashes, a question). The hold is bounded — after a policy-named wait with the belt still shut, the park with both readings is the honest ending.

## Implementation

Where: fleet/core/src/item/advance.rs — the reviewer spawn after `item.delivered` and the fresh-builder spawn after `item.returned` both park the item when the `Seats` seam's spawn refuses; the belt's refusal is built in fleet/controller/src/transient.rs (`refusal`, the two-line reading of load and seats mid-turn) and reaches core as a plain refusal string.

Change: the seam's refusal carries a kind — `Belt` (load or seats over the ceiling, a reading about this minute) or `Refused` (anything else). On `Belt` the act HOLDS: the standing stays Delivered or Returned, a note `SPAWN HELD — <the two belt lines>` is written once (not per pass), and the next pass retries; a policy key `[core.flight] hold_passes` (default 60, five minutes at the 5 s poll) bounds it, after which the park is written with both readings as today. Every other refusal parks as before.

Test, in advance's tests with the rig's belt seam: a spawn refused `Belt` on the first pass and admitted on the second — the item is never parked and `item.dispatched` for the reviewer follows on pass two; a second arm holds the belt shut past `hold_passes` and reads the park with the belt's two lines. Red proof: the hold removed, the first arm reads `item.parked` on pass one, as the rehearsal did twice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reviewer spawn refused by the load ceiling leaves the item delivered and unparked, and a later pass under the ceiling spawns the reviewer, proved by an arm whose belt seam reads over-then-under.
- A red proof: the hold removed, the arm reads item.parked on the first refusal.
- Gate: touched suites green; reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

title: the flight's seat cap is read off a fold computed once per advance pass, so one pass dispatches every ready item — four seats spawned under max_seats = 2 on tinytown-41z31
description:
## Re-measured 2026-09-16 (author, tree b2db5ee27) — one clause corrected, and the change is wider than a counter

advance.rs is byte-identical to the spec's base: mid_flight is counted off the once-per-pass fold at :478 and compared at :487-488 against seat_cap (:736), and the comment at :350-352 says nothing below rewrites the fold. The corrected clause: "the reviewer spawn and the return's fresh-builder spawn read the same fold" is false — seat_cap has ONE call site, :487 inside dispatch_act; spawn_the_reviewer (:1503) and the return's spawn (:1740-1799) consult no cap at all, and the crash re-dispatch (:872) does not either. So the Implementation is: a pass-local count of seats spent, incremented at every seat-spending act, AND a cap comparison ADDED at the three sites that have none, each parking or holding exactly as a dispatch over the cap does (the dispatch site's own hold precedent is at :584-590). The rig takes the cap (fleet/core/tests/advance.rs:515 seats: Option<u64>; :569-570 writes seats = N into inputs), and the existing arm at :1035 is the neighbour; AC1's four ready items under seats = 2 runs as written, and a second arm covers a reviewer spawn and a return spawn under a full cap.

---

## Why

Found at the rehearsal's step 18 (tinytown-tnkuq.20, 2026-09-14): flight tinytown-41z31 was pinned at seats = 2 (inputs.toml, from [core.flight] max_seats = 2) and the controller dispatched all four items to four spawned seats inside one advance pass, 07:18:19Z to 07:18:37Z (item.dispatched at seq 28, 33, 38, 43), so the box carried four builder sessions and their gates where the policy said two.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. With `[core.flight] max_seats = 2`, plan four ready items and `fleet fly`.
2. Read the stream: four `item.dispatched` lines inside one pass (07:18:25Z to 07:18:37Z on tinytown-41z31), four transient worktrees cut, four sessions started.
3. Expected: two dispatched, the third only after a terminal event on one of them.

## What was measured

fleet/core/src/item/advance.rs, dispatch_act: the cap compares `mid_flight` — the count of standings in Dispatched, Reviewing or Crashed — against seat_cap(inputs). `standings` is the fold computed once at the top of the pass, so inside one pass every item reads the same count the pass started with (zero here), and the cap is met only on the NEXT pass, after the fold has caught up. The cap holds across passes and not within one; a flight whose items all stand ready at takeoff dispatches every one of them.

## What

The count the cap reads includes the dispatches this pass has already made: a pass-local counter incremented at each item.dispatched (and each reviewer spawn), added to the fold's mid-flight count before the comparison; or the pass dispatches at most (cap - mid_flight) items and stops. The fold stays the record; the counter is the pass's own memory of what it just spent.

## Implementation

Where: fleet/core/src/item/advance.rs, `dispatch_act` — `mid_flight` counts standings in Dispatched, Reviewing or Crashed off the fold `standings`, computed once at the top of the pass; the reviewer spawn and the return's fresh-builder spawn read the same fold.

Change: a pass-local `spent: u64` carried through the pass (a field on the pass's own state, or a `Cell` beside `standings`), incremented at every seat-spending act this pass makes — an item dispatch, a reviewer spawn, a return's re-dispatch, a crash's re-dispatch — and added to `mid_flight` before every cap comparison. The cap then holds within a pass as well as across passes; nothing about the fold changes.

Test, beside the existing cap arm in advance's tests: four ready items under `seats = 2` — the first pass writes exactly two `item.dispatched`; a terminal event on one of them (the rig's stub delivers) lets the next pass dispatch the third. Red proof: the counter removed, the first pass writes four.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A flight of four ready items under seats = 2 dispatches two in the first pass and the third only after a terminal event frees a seat, proved by an arm reading item.dispatched stamps against the step.closed that precedes the third.
- A red proof: the pass-local count removed, the arm reads four dispatches in one pass.
- Gate: touched suites green; reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

title: fleet's suite in minutes and hermetic: the cli verbs' per-call bd cost, a fresh baseline, and a test run that can never reach the live fleet instance beside it
description:
## Why

Two goals, unchanged since the epic was filed in tinytown (2026-09-13, Alberto's order): fleet's suite runs in minutes rather than the better part of an hour, and a test run can never reach the live fleet instance it is running beside (fleet builds fleet). Rewritten 2026-09-23 after the split: the measurements, the gate and the process the original description stood on stayed in tinytown; the original text is preserved in this bead's notes.

## Where it stands in tinyfleet

- Hermetic: what came over is tools/dolt-test-server, tools/rig-env-check, and the FLEET_TEST_DOLT_PORT rule in core/tests/common/board.rs. Open gap: fleet-6eb1o (fixtures read the person's global git excludes file).
- Two tiers (fleet-6ravv.4): the core half is done. Store::export is on the trait, the fake implements it, core/tests/contract.rs runs one contract against both stores, and core's verb suites run on test_support::Board. What is left is the cli verb binaries (deliver, dispatch, run, item_json, seat, routines), which still build real bd boards through cli/tests/common/mod.rs.
- No current measurement. target/nextest/default/junit.xml predates the split: it still carries fleet-cli::flight, which no longer exists. Take a fresh baseline before quoting any number.
- No gate. tinytown's Makefile (fleet-fmt/check/test/ring), its fleet.toml budget key (suites.fleet_test_budget_seconds) and the load-before verdict did not come over. README.md "Working here" and the header of .config/nextest.toml still describe them.

## Open question (Alberto's)

Does tinyfleet get a runner (Makefile, justfile or xtask) and a budget gate again, and at what number? That decision decides how the survivors (fleet-6ravv.4, fleet-ja29t, fleet-eqi3r) are judged.

## Done when

- a fresh baseline is measured and recorded here;
- fleet-6ravv.4's cli tier has landed;

Those are different experiments on different axes. A served board wins when many callers share one engine, because embedded callers each pay their own engine start; it loses when the box is busy with work that is not the suite's, because the server competes for cores it does not share with its caller. Both readings are true in their own cell.

THE MEASUREMENTS THE EPIC STANDS ON (architect-2, 2026-09-12/13, this box):
- one make fleet-test: 980 s of tests over 49 binaries run one after another, 763 arms; build 10 s warm; clippy 3 s (builder-1's gate log on tinytown-tnkuq.47)

2. the rig invariant — HOME, FLEET_DIR and FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN set to the rig's own tmp unconditionally, pinned by a drift arm

Plus the beads already open on the same problem, moved under this epic in the same act and listed in the notes.

title: fleet: a stub-agent seam for a seat that COMMITS and then dies, and the live crash re-dispatch arm on it (tinytown-tnkuq.73's AC2)
notes:
Filed by builder-2 at the review of tinytown-tnkuq.73, 2026-09-13, on Alberto's ruling in session: land tinytown-tnkuq.73's AC1 and AC3 and carry AC2 here.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD. tinytown-tnkuq.73's AC2 asks for the crash re-dispatch proved live on the scratch project through the shipped binary: a stub builder that commits one file and then exits mid-turn, whose re-dispatched successor's worktree HEAD equals that commit. It could not be built inside that slice because THE SEAM DOES NOT EXIST, measured at 6f9143908: fleet/cli/tests/flight.rs carries exactly two stub behaviours, logged-out (with logged-out-live) and kill-when-assigned, and the word crash does not occur in that file at all — control: it occurs in fleet/cli/tests/drive.rs and fleet/cli/tests/workspace.rs, so the read is absence and not a broken needle. kill-when-assigned dies BEFORE any commit, which is the one thing AC2's case cannot be: the re-dispatch cuts from the branch's last commit, so the seat must have committed first.

WHAT LANDS HERE. A stub-agent behaviour that commits a file and then exits in a way the controller writes session.crashed for, and the live arm on it. The seam is the reusable half — every later crash arm wants it, and tinytown-tnkuq.20's rehearsal exercises the same path.

COST, measured on this box 2026-09-13, so nobody plans this as a small one: fleet-cli flight arms run 8 to 30 minutes each; the full suite is 832 arms in 1653s with 67 already marked slow.

A FLAKE TO FIX OR AVOID IN THE SAME NEIGHBOURHOOD, found while building tinytown-tnkuq.73: fleet-cli::flight::a_loop_killed_between_a_dispatch_and_its_event_restarts_without_dispatching_twice hung 102 minutes against a 494s baseline. Its fixture carries 7 events and no session.crashed at all, and its stub builder lost a git add race so fleet deliver answered 'nothing is staged' 120 times. Not this bead's subject, but it is the arm nearest to the one being written.

THE HONEST PART: tinytown-tnkuq.73's readiness pass, written by this seat, answered READY 3 yes. READY 3 asks that every criterion name the command and the exit code that proves it. AC2 names a live arm whose fixture does not exist, so it was not provable as written and the pass should have caught it. Recorded here because the next readiness pass on a live arm should ask whether the seam it needs is on the tree.
HELD (architect-2, 2026-09-17, tinytown-tnkuq.92): deferred, not closed. This defect lives in the flight's advance or fly machinery, which the fleet-layers direction turns into the core run lifecycle (pin, lock, cap, resume, retire-all) with composition moving to tiny's workflows. Whether this code survives, moves or is replaced is the workflows sitting's to say; the bug is real and measured and comes back to open if the code it names survives the MVP. Deferred so the ready pool stops offering work on code whose fate is undecided.
Moved from the tinytown board on 2026-09-22, where it was tinytown-ppjwc; that bead is closed there with a pointer here. Edges to beads that stayed on the tinytown board, not carried across: discovered-from tinytown-tnkuq.73.
close_reason: Obsolete: deferred until it was known whether the code it names survives the MVP. It did not: the flight advance and fleet fly/plan/autopilot left core at tinytown fd7f6a47a (2026-09-17; see core/src/lib.rs:83). The crash re-dispatch arm it seams for belonged to the advance. If the run lifecycle grows crash re-dispatch, carry the need for a commit-then-die stub seam into that design (see closed fleet-biilb).

title: [epic] fleet, built in-house: the controller and the plugin shape in fleet/ until the phase-A gate — the lessons documents, the scaffold, the PRD's five slices — every fleet bead until the leave (Alberto's D8 on tinytown-ui3u9, 2026-09-05; brain/fleet-migration.md §5 A2–A4)
description:
## Why

Alberto's ruling 2026-09-05 (D8 on tinytown-ui3u9, verbatim option label "All of fleet in-house; gc after it leaves"): fleet — the controller, the cli and the packs — is built by tinytown's own seats in fleet/ at this repo's root, on this board, until it can build itself and leaves for Tinytown/fleet as one snapshot (D10). brain/fleet-migration.md §5 A2–A4 is the sequence; the fleet-controller PRD at fleet/docs/prds/fleet-controller-prd.md is what the slices build. This epic holds every fleet bead until the leave; the fleet label is the queue (bd list --label fleet).

## What

Children, in landing order — each one bead wide until its prerequisite has landed (brain/architect-role.md, the fan-out rule): the lessons documents (A2 step 2), the scaffold (A2 step 3), then the PRD's slices 1–5 and the plugin shape (A4), each a spec bead by an architect. The phase-A gate closes the epic: fleet's controller starts a builder, observes it to delivery and retires it, on a fleet bead, with the porter untouched (plan §5 A4, the gate).

## Rules for every child

- Nothing under fleet/ references tinytown: no bead id, no path, no seat name; grep -rci tinytown fleet/ reads 0 at every landing (Alberto, 2026-09-05, on tinytown-tvw64). Commit subjects carry the bead id by house rule and never leave (plan §5 B0).
- Written new, the porter read and never copied (D6); the lessons documents are read before the PRD's requirement is built.
- Stdlib-class dependencies only (PRD Q1): a TOML reader and a JSON writer are the only crates permitted.
- Gate line on every child: touched suites green; reviewer runs the full suite at landing.

## Success Criteria

- SC1 The phase-A gate as brain/fleet-migration.md §5 A4 states it: fleet's controller, a second user service beside the porter, dispatches a fleet bead to a builder it started, observes it to delivery and retires it, once in auto mode and once under dontAsk, with the porter untouched — recorded on the closing child with the projection and event-stream excerpts that prove each verb.
- SC2 Every child landed through tools/land with its fleetmake rows green; grep -rci tinytown fleet/ reads 0 on main at the close.
- SC3 The leave (plan §5 B0) is filed as its own bead, discovered-from this epic, before this epic closes.
notes:
CHILDREN FILED (architect-1, 2026-09-05, under tinytown-gmkie, Alberto's order for the phase-A board): tinytown-tnkuq.4–.9 (controller slices 2–5, install and create, the self-build gate), .10–.16 (core: format and registry, guards, dispatch and brief, deliver and review, land, core's first gate, fly and autopilot), .17 (the plugin shape), .19 (tinytown's project.toml), .20 (the rehearsal), .23 (the switch), .24 (the tiny-fleet pack). Every one a FRAME owing its SPEC PASS and readiness pass before dispatch. Blocks edges child-to-child along the two spines only.

SC1 RE-READ under D12 (Alberto, 2026-09-05, tinytown-gmkie): the epic closes at the REHEARSAL (tinytown-tnkuq.20 — fleet flies one national flight of tinytown beads with the porter stopped), not at the self-build gate; the self-build gate (tinytown-tnkuq.9) and core's first gate (tinytown-tnkuq.15) are gates inside the phase. SC3 is met by tinytown-tnkuq.23 (the switch), filed as a child rather than a discovered-from sibling. brain/departure-board.md lays the children out as flights 1–10.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08, in architect-2's session, mechanism: fleet-workspace-shape, verbatim): "the workspace with three crates and one binary it is" — the cli is not a separate project: a Cargo workspace at fleet/ with fleet-core, fleet-controller and a thin fleet cli crate producing the one fleet binary; the options and the application are on tinytown-tnkuq.10, whose Why reserved the decision, and the workspace scaffold is filed as a child of this epic and .10's prerequisite (this note's next line names it).
The workspace scaffold is tinytown-tnkuq.25; tinytown-tnkuq.10 now depends on it.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T17:36Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-start-stop-and-status, verbatim): "fleet start | stop: should start and stop the controller" and "fleet runway: can be folder into status"
The seat's reading, for the cli PRD this session is drafting: fleet start loads the installed user service and fleet stop unloads it — the "load is a second deliberate act" the controller PRD's install requirement reserves, given its verb pair; fleet install writes and never starts, as before. fleet runway is not a command: its reading (each seat's context against the rest threshold, the window left) is a section of fleet status, which already prints the projection and the switch. Both apply to the frames tinytown-tnkuq.8 (install and create) and tinytown-tnkuq.16 (status) at their spec passes.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T17:49Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-nouns-seat-and-event, verbatim): "fleet clear-halt: sounds good" (to folding it under fleet event); "feed spawn: can it live under fleet seat spawn?"; "fleet retire: same as above fleet seat retire?"; "fleet install: could this be done as part of the command that installs fleet itself? this gets into how fleet is installed which is a different conversation. this could also run the first time that fleet start is invoked. pi uses `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh` for install"; "fleet fly and prime: look good"; "fleet courier: i like that you used ring in that sentence. i guess either ping or ring could work, your choice."
The seat's reading, for the cli PRD: two nouns. fleet seat is what is DONE to a seat — fleet seat spawn --first-turn, fleet seat feed <seat> --first-turn, fleet seat retire <seat> [--dead] (controller PRD R30–R32 unchanged in substance; tinytown-tnkuq.7's frame renames), and fleet seat ring <seat> --text (the packs PRD's P1 courier; ring chosen over ping because a ring is a doorbell and carries no authority, the fleet's own word for it). fleet event is what a seat SAYS — woke|rest|handed-off|exited, and now clear-halt <seat> as the person's request the controller consumes on its tick (controller PRD R14's remedy; spelled clear-halt and not revive, because revive is already the controller's own verdict for adopt-in-place and one word for two things is the drift this harness exists to catch). fleet install leaves the command surface: its work — the user service written, the machine directory created, telemetry asked — runs either inside the installer script or on the first fleet start, decided in the install conversation Alberto named; tinytown-tnkuq.8's frame carries this note at its spec pass. fleet fly, fleet autopilot and fleet prime stand as listed.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T17:52Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-item-and-verb-shape, AskUserQuestion answers verbatim): "item (Recommended)" for the word the verbs act on — "we need to settle on a name for beads that is not beads … beads is both too specific (we could support other memory layers in the future) and abstract (there are formulas and memory beads under it)"; and "Top-level: fleet dispatch <item> (Recommended)" for the verb shape.
The seat's reading, for the cli PRD: the work unit is an ITEM everywhere a person reads — help text, notes, the flight record — and the id the verbs take is an item id; bd stays the store beneath it and is named only where the store itself is meant. The four verbs and brief are top-level words: fleet dispatch <item>, fleet brief <item>, fleet deliver, fleet review <item>, fleet land <item>; fleet fly and fleet autopilot on|off beside them. Declined: task (collides with bd's issue type), work (no count noun), cargo (the analogy, and the Rust tool's name), and nesting the four under an item noun (symmetry bought with length on the most-typed verbs). Alberto's standing instruction for the PRD, verbatim: "i just want to make sure every command is explained in detail".
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T17:57Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-surface-closed, verbatim): "great lets add those two as well. fleet observe: lgtm / fleet event: lgtm / fleet doctor: lgtm / fleet pack search: lgtm / fleet --version: lgtm"
The seat's reading, closing the cli PRD's command inventory: fleet pack gains remove <source> (deletes the pack directory and drops its packs.lock table keyed by the source as typed; refuses core and any pack another installed pack imports) and list (packs.lock as a table — source, version, commit, fetched). fleet observe [--once] stays as the foreground form of the controller loop beside start and stop. fleet event carries the writers (woke|rest|handed-off|exited, clear-halt) and the readers (tail [--follow] [--since <seq>] [--seat] [--type], show <id>); the readers are a frame of their own. fleet doctor (P1) and fleet pack search (P2) stand as the PRDs place them. fleet --version stays. Surface at this note: nine families — lifecycle (create, start, stop, status), seat (spawn, feed, retire, ring), event (six writers and readers), item verbs (dispatch, brief, deliver, review, land), flight (fly, autopilot), hooks (guard, prime), orders (list, check, run, history), packs (add, check, remove, list, search), and observe with --version. Standing instruction for the PRD text: every command explained in detail.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T18:06Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-nudge-not-ring, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim: "nudge (Recommended)"): the courier verb is fleet seat nudge <seat> --text. The naming doc's row for waking a live seat with a message already reads nudge and lists courier among the coinages not carried over, so ring — chosen earlier in this sitting and recorded under cli-nouns-seat-and-event — is withdrawn: one word for one mechanism, the controller's threshold nudge and the person's message on the same adapter path. tinytown-tnkuq.34 is retitled.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T18:30Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cli-ui-crates, verbatim): "document somewhere or file a bead for flight 5. indicatif for progress on fly and land, console for styled status lines, dialoguer for create's two questions"
The seat's reading: filed as tinytown-tnkuq.36 on flight 5, the three crates entering fleet-cli through one ui module with a stated policy (plain on a pipe, NO_COLOR or a dumb terminal; progress on stderr past two seconds; prompts refuse a pipe naming the flag), first uses on the verbs built today, and the fly, land and create frames carrying a note each naming the surface they take. comfy-table not taken; ratatui is the manager's question and not the cli's.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T18:58Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: manager-api-shape, verbatim): "If fleet publishes one, it should be generated from the same Rust types the cli uses, with a crate such as utoipa deriving the schema from the handlers, so the cli and the API cannot disagree, and it should be a handful of paths, loopback by default, over the two files that are already the record"
The seat's reading: settled ahead of the manager's design session, filed as fleet-tnkuq.37 under this epic — one definition of the surface in Rust types shared by the cli and the API, the schema generated and never hand-written, a small path count, loopback unless turned on, every read from the projection and the event stream; the SSE transport of the controller PRD's P1 is the stream's network form. The sitting decides where the manager runs, its paths, its writes, its exposure, its screen and the premium line (Q1–Q6 on the bead).
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T19:45Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: log-and-stats-one-prd, verbatim): "ok so log and stats deserver their own prds or maybe one prd for both since they're part of the same story"
The seat's reading: one PRD for the two, filed as fleet-tnkuq.38 under this epic — the record as a product and the numbers folded over it, because stats has no input but the log; the settled list and the seven questions are on the bead. Off the departure board: the log and stats are pieces after phase A, like the manager.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: vision-primitives-not-features, AskUserQuestion clarification verbatim): "Primitives, not features" — the vision page's "Primitives, not a platform" bullet is retitled to that heading, the phrase pi.dev leads its own extensibility section with, chosen after reading that page as the reference for how fleet should feel: a foundation that unlocks customization on top. Declined: "A foundation, not a framework" (the seat's recommendation), keeping the old heading with a rewritten body, and "Simple, local, and truly yours" as the heading (that line leads fleet/docs/integrations.md instead). The body under the new heading and the integrations page that is its long form land together on the bead filed for the page.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-is-the-name, verbatim): "cockpit it is, great." — the piece the vision page calls fleet-manager is named cockpit: the product's fourth flying word, allowed under the naming doc's rule because the content is an instrument panel (a bar of gauges and alerts, a status readout, a seat held while autopilot flies) and it is used everywhere without variation. The rename touches the vision page, the naming doc's row for the screen, and the design bead's title, and lands with the cockpit PRD. Declined: manager (plain, says nothing, collides with the job title and with process managers).
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-server-in-the-binary, verbatim): "where the server goes is a great question. i'll take your recommendation here. my only request is that it should behave similar to docker. the app can be closed while the server is still running and you would see the fleet icon up on the notification bar with a menu that has items like quit server, stop controller, open cockpit. the server should be able to run even if the app is not open." — the recommendation taken: the typed API's handlers live in one library crate; the one binary gains a serve verb that runs them over HTTP on loopback, so a headless box serves a phone with no window; the cockpit is a web app in a Tauri shell that calls the same handlers as Tauri commands on the desktop and embeds the server. The Docker Desktop shape is the requirement: closing the window leaves the server running, a fleet icon sits in the menu bar (macOS) or the system tray (Linux) with at least quit server, stop controller and open cockpit, and the server runs with no app open. Declined: an HTTP surface in the controller (the controller PRD's non-goal stands); a separate product that only reads the two files.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-economy-warning, verbatim): "economy: i meant the economy.level in fleet.toml" — the economy warning in the cockpit's settings screen is against dialing economy.level (SM | MD | LG, the reference's spend dial, brain/harness/fleet.md) up when the account runway will not reach the horizon; the cap on concurrent flights is the same reading's other arm. The seat's reading: economy.level enters the fleet's fleet.toml as a policy key the cockpit reads and writes, the runway reading is an adapter measurement of account usage folded with the stream's cost events (the log-and-stats sitting's cost question), the warning is the cockpit's before a save, and the refusal is fly's and the autopilot pull's — the cockpit shows the record and holds no belief of its own.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-serve-and-launch, verbatim): "the app's first launch just like docker when you launch the mac app. you should also be able to launch via fleet serve with the icon appearing in the bar but the app itself not launching" — launching the cockpit app starts the server the way Docker Desktop's first launch starts its daemon, and fleet serve from a shell starts the server with the menu-bar icon shown and no window opened. The seat's reading: the server and the tray icon are one resident process with two modes, tray-only and windowed; fleet serve starts it tray-only, launching the app starts it windowed or shows the window of the one already running, and both are idempotent; the window is a view over the resident process and closing it returns to tray-only. The resident process is the login-item shape, so a closet machine serves a phone across a reboot. Build question left for the PRD, with the seat's recommendation: the cockpit app is the resident process and fleet serve starts it in tray mode, so the fleet binary links no GUI toolkit and a display-less box takes a no-tray flag; declined by recommendation only, not by ruling: the tray drawn by the fleet binary itself.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-read-paths, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim): "#2 but i want to explain why, one view of the cockpit will be a task management feature similar to Linear but built for beads and agent orchestration" — Q2 of the manager bead: the four paths over the two files (status, events, stats, config) PLUS an item family reading the work graph, because one cockpit view is task management over the work graph itself. The seat's reading: the four verbs gain item events regardless (dispatched, delivered, reviewed, landed, returned, decision owed), since the stream is what the phone tails and what stats fold; the item family is more than one GET — a task view needs list and query (ready, blocked, by label, by assignee, the dependency edges) — and its types cannot be shared with bd's, which is Go, so they are fleet's Rust types over bd's --json output, the one place the "same types as the cli" rule reaches a store fleet does not own. Declined: the four alone with no item path; two paths.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-writes, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim): "The full verb surface" — Q3 of the manager bead: the API writes settings (policy keys to fleet.toml, machine keys such as accounts to the machine directory, never committed), autopilot on|off, an answer to a decision, and the verbs — dispatch, fly, nudge, retire — each through the handler the cli already has, so the API adds no writer of its own and every write reads itself back and exits by the one table. With the task view (cockpit-read-paths) the item family writes too: create, update, claim, close, dep add, through bd. Declined: read-only; the three writes alone.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-exposure, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim): "Loopback, LAN by key with a paired token (Recommended)" — Q4 of the manager bead: loopback by default; one machine-local key binds the LAN; a token generated at first serve is paired from the settings screen by QR and carried by the phone; a remote bridge, if one exists, is a relay of the same server. Declined: off-machine only through a bridge; LAN open with no auth.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-premium-line, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim): "tbd, we shouldnt gate mobile access behind a paid tier" — Q6 of the manager bead stays open, with one constraint ruled: mobile access is never behind a paid tier. The vision page's sentence "The premium tier adds a bridge to your phone" and the fleet-manager section's "the door to the premium tier" no longer hold as written and are edited when the cockpit PRD lands. Declined: any second device as premium; the app itself as premium.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-09, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-view-line, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim: "Two tiers, no iframe (Recommended)", taken after a survey of twelve tools on fleet-tnkuq.37 and a closer read of pi.dev's slot-and-kit model): custom views in the cockpit have two tiers and no iframe. Tier one — views as declarative documents over a cockpit block vocabulary (list, table, board, gauge, timeline, detail, form, markdown, action at filing; the vocabulary grows with demand) bound to the API's typed paths and stream queries, rendered by the cockpit inside named slots the app owns, validated by a check verb, shipped in a pack, picked up from a file with no build step. Tier two — custom components as web components composed from the cockpit's own component library and semantic theme tokens, rendered in the page and never in a frame, with a check that refuses a component carrying a raw color, font or size. Taken from pi.dev whole: the slot model, the theme as semantic names an author uses and never sets, no build step and reload from a file, and "ask your seat to build it". Not taken: pi's free enforcement, which the terminal medium supplies and the web does not — hence the check. Declined: pi's model as is (code only); declarative only; three tiers with a sandboxed iframe (every rung-five host has the failure Alberto named: nothing but words keeps it on theme).
DATE CORRECTION (architect-2, 2026-09-08T22:33Z read from date -u): every note this seat wrote on this record today carrying the date 2026-09-09 — the rulings vision-primitives-not-features, cockpit-is-the-name, cockpit-server-in-the-binary, cockpit-serve-and-launch, cockpit-economy-warning, cockpit-read-paths, cockpit-writes, cockpit-exposure, cockpit-premium-line and cockpit-view-line on the epic, the sitting-opened, survey-opened and survey-findings notes on fleet-tnkuq.37, and the description and verdict on tinytown-tnkuq.39 — was written on 2026-09-08 between roughly 20:30Z and 22:30Z. The date was taken from the harness's own "today" line instead of the clock; the clock reads 2026-09-08. The content of every note stands; only the date in each is wrong by one day.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T22:43Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-attach-in-a-pane, verbatim): "it should open a pane inside the cockpit. we will define what a pane is down the road and how extensions can also leverage them" — the roster's attach opens the seat's conversation in a pane inside the cockpit, never in the user's tmux server or a separate terminal window. A pane is a cockpit primitive to be defined later, one that extensions can also use — so it joins the slot list the view-line ruling (cockpit-view-line) says the app owns, and the attach pane is its first occupant. The seat's reading: this makes attach a terminal surface inside a web view (a terminal emulator in the pane driven by the adapter's attach), which is the largest shape named on the design bead; tmux disappears as a requirement and the terminal policy key with it. Declined: the user's tmux server; a new terminal window.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T22:44Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: cockpit-views-core-vs-tiny-fleet, verbatim): "once we get closer to building the cockpit we will hash out the details. there's one more thing related to this i want documented somewhere and that's the views that belong in the core pack vs what belongs in the tiny-fleet pack. also what should we name the folder that houses theses extensions inside a pack? what do others call it? each of these will be their own epic down the road since they're a huge amount of work / part of core: - Tasks (beads): linear for beads, inbox, filters, views, create beads using an agent window - Schedule (orders): see upcoming + past, edit, add - in V2 -> Review: git history, review commit later, diff, PRs, approve, decline, etc. (the idea here is to completely replace vscode and beadazzle as tools i have to jump between) / part of tiny-fleet: - Flights (runs): the departure board, currently flying and upcoming ones, this is the one feature that's opinionated about how the user should work. this is probably where creating and editing formulas will also live since it dictates what the flights do". The split as ruled: core's views are Tasks (the work graph as a Linear-shaped task manager: inbox, filters, saved views, creating items through an agent window), Schedule (orders: upcoming and past, edit, add) and, at V2, Review (git history, a commit's diff, PRs, approve and decline — the cockpit replacing the editor and the bd screen as places to jump between); tiny-fleet's view is Flights (runs: the departure board, what is flying and what is next, and where formulas are created and edited, since formulas dictate what a flight does) — the one view with an opinion about how a person should work, which is why it is a pack's. Each family is its own epic later. The home for this is the cockpit PRD (fleet-tnkuq.37 AC1), with the integrations page's pack section owing one sentence when it lands.
RULING (Alberto, 2026-09-08T22:47Z, in architect-2's session, mechanism: pack-views-slot, AskUserQuestion answer verbatim: "views/ (Recommended)"): the pack folder that houses cockpit views is views/ — a ninth slot, fleet's own addition to Gas City's eight, chosen as the word VS Code (contributes.views), Obsidian (ItemView), Slack (views.publish), Raycast (root views) and Linear (custom views) share; Gas City's format has no slot for a screen, so nothing collides. title: a takeoff run that fails reaches nobody: fleet status has no runs section and the morning skill reads only gates, but the takeoff skill says `fleet status` shows the run
description:
## What

packs/tiny/skills/takeoff/SKILL.md:83-84 says '`fleet status` shows it'. But status's whole page (cli/src/status.rs:256-302) prints roster, in-flight, effects, context, rules and routines, and the Projection has no runs field (controller/src/projection.rs:24-60). A run that exits 1 (for example when `fleet land` refuses inside takeoff) writes `run.failed` and closes its record item with no gate (core/src/item/run.rs:206-233). The morning skill reads only `bd gate list` (packs/tiny/skills/morning/SKILL.md:37-41). So a failed overnight flight shows up in no instrument a person reads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 `fleet status` gains a runs section (open, waiting, failed since the last read, parked) with the gate count. At minimum: the takeoff skill line is corrected, and the morning skill reads `run.failed` and `run.could_not_tell` from the stream.
- AC2 An arm where a run exits 1, and the run shows up where the person reads.
- Open question (not this bead's to rule): whether a push on run.failed or a park ships as a tiny routine before the manager (fleet-tnkuq.37).

## Source

Carried from tinytown-v0y1v (the silent-stop postmortem of 2026-09-06) (closed on the tinytown board at the 2026-09-22 post-harness sweep; listed in tinyfleet-review.md), triaged against tinyfleet HEAD 44c3736 on 2026-09-23.

title: the record guard's bare-id shape is exactly four characters, and none of this board's suffixes is four — the check never refuses a real fleet id
description:
## What

core/src/guard/record.rs:286-290 `stem_is_a_suffix` requires `stem.chars().count() == 4`, plus at least one digit and one lowercase letter; the docstring at :245-253 says the same. The guard reads no board, so this fixed shape is its whole precision. bd lengthens suffixes as a board grows: this board's live suffixes are 3 (fleet-wnt, fleet-mdw), 5 (most) and 6 (fleet-6ywp53), none of them 4. So `bd note x "see 6ravv"` passes the bare-id check. The tests (core/tests/guard.rs:488-535) use only `a1b2`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 One refused row per suffix length 3, 5 and 6, plus a full `<prefix>-6ravv` row that is not refused.
- AC2 The ordinary-prose and year rows stay green. Before choosing a range (3 to 6, or bd's own generator ceiling), measure the false-positive rate over this board's notes, or check against real ids.
- AC3 The record.rs docstring states the new shape.

description:
## Why

What it still parented is ordinary product backlog that brain/fleet-layers.md places after the MVP (the ordering around fleet-layers.md:550-585).

## What

- the fleet manager design (brain/fleet-layers.md § API, § Views, Q16)

title: Autopilot as a routine: a machine setting read and written through fleet settings (fleet-layers Q12, ruled A), and a routine on a schedule whose guard reads it and opens the oldest plan while the open runs are under the cap — the switch's new home after plan, fly and autopilot left core
description:
## Why

fleet-layers Q12 (ruled 2026-09-17, A): autopilot's home is a machine setting, read and written through the API, by fleet settings or the cockpit's screen — machine state, not policy, not process environment. tinytown-tnkuq.94 removed fleet autopilot and the switch file from core with plan and fly; unattended composition is tiny's takeoff workflow over fleet run (tinytown-tnkuq.110, flown). The board's line "filed when .110 has flown" is this bead. fleet-layers § What tiny ships on day one places autopilot as a routine AFTER day one, so this is not on the switch's road; it is filed so the requirement is not discoverable only by tripping over it.

## What (frame)

A settings verb (fleet settings get|set <key>) over a file in the machine directory; the key autopilot with values on and off; a routine in tiny (packs/tiny/orders or routines) on a schedule whose guard reads the setting through the API and, when on, opens the oldest plan while the open runs are under the cap ([core.run] or the routine's own cap) — never while a run is open above it; off, nothing opens. Alberto's standing order stands over it: the switch is OFF while he is asleep or absent.

## Acceptance Criteria (frame — finalized by the spec pass)

fleet settings set autopilot on|off round-trips; the routine's guard reads it; with on and no open run the oldest plan opens once; with off nothing opens; the cap holds.

## Risk

After the MVP and after the switch; owes a spec pass.
